issues.note: Entry-level label covers every sense; house rule forbids repeating it at sense level.
Verb is not a real confusable for compare; preposition replacement is debatable.
Naming English is not targeting a language; an example is not a duplicating note.
Natural classroom sentence; "in this sentence" states no general rule.
Content noun needs no explanation field; what adverbs modify belongs in the definition.
Examples may illustrate; adaptation note partly overlaps them, a small real point.
Definition misses frequency adverbs and sentence adverbs, a major gap.

findings.F1: An explanation field is used on a content noun, carrying what adverbs modify instead of the definition.
findings.F2: The definition's list (how, when, where, how much) omits frequency (always, never) and sentence-level adverbs.

missed: The learner error (I like very much coffee) is about adverb placement in general, not an error learners make with the word adverb; the grammar adaptation note likewise describes adverb formation rather than a trap in translating the noun adverb.
